_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED FROM THE PINNED UPSTREAM SCHEMA. This is NOT a capture.
Transcribed from `codex app-server generate-json-schema` as emitted by
codex-cli 0.153.4 (~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/bin/codex, the
binary this box spawns), file v2/TurnCompletedNotification.json. No codex
turn was run to produce it: the only machine available here is production,
and #1255 forbids running real turns on it.
Shape: { threadId, turn: Turn }. Turn = { id, status, error, startedAt,
completedAt, durationMs, items, itemsView }; required: id, items, status.
TurnStatus enum: completed | interrupted | failed | inProgress.
TurnError = { message (required), codexErrorInfo?, additionalDetails?,
misalignment? }; `error` is 'only populated when the Turn's status is failed'.
CodexErrorInfo is a oneOf: EITHER a bare string from the enum
[contextWindowExceeded, sessionBudgetExceeded, usageLimitExceeded,
rateLimitExceeded, serverOverloaded, cyberPolicy, misalignmentPolicyViolation,
internalServerError, unauthorized, badRequest, threadRollbackFailed,
sandboxError, other] OR a single-key object such as
{ "httpConnectionFailed": { "httpStatusCode": 502 } } (also
responseStreamConnectionFailed, responseStreamDisconnected,
responseTooManyFailedAttempts, activeTurnNotSteerable). Every spelling is
camelCase on the app-server wire, as `threadId` / `durationMs` here are.
`startedAt` / `completedAt` are Unix SECONDS (int64), not milliseconds.
`items` and `itemsView` are transcribed so the kernel test can prove they are
STRIPPED from the stored row: every item already has rows of its own.
`threadId` here is a PLACEHOLDER and is not part of the transcription. The
kernel's `on_notification` prologue drops any notification whose `threadId` is
not the harness's current thread, so the test substitutes its own seeded id
(`SEED_THREAD_ID` in tests/cases/planner_harness_items_persist.rs) over this
value before emitting the frame.
Once #1625 P1 ships, `SELECT params FROM harness_items WHERE
method='turn/completed' AND json_extract(params,'$.status')='failed'` on a
production DB promotes this to a captured payload.
